'''''The Engineer''''' is a London-based monthly magazine and website covering the latest developments and business news in [[engineering]] and technology in the UK<ref>{{cite book|title=Writers' & Artists' Yearbook 2017|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_knOCwAAQBAJ&pg=PA54|access-date=24 October 2016|date=28 July 2016|publisher=Bloomsbury Publishing|isbn=978-1-4729-2866-5|page=54}}</ref> and internationally.

==History and description==
''The Engineer'' was founded in January 1856. It was established by Edward Charles Healey, an entrepreneur and engineering enthusiast with financial interests in the railways whose friends included [[Robert Stephenson]] and [[Isambard Kingdom Brunel]].  The journal was created as a technical magazine for engineers.<ref name="his">{{citation|title=History of "The Engineer"|url=https://theengineer.markallengroup.com/production/content/uploads/2012/07/history-of-The-Engineer.pdf|work=The Engineer|volume=(Centenary Number) 4 January 1956|pages=146–148}}</ref>

''The Engineer'' began covering  engineering including inventions and patents during a high point of British economic manufacturing power. In the 19th century it also published stock prices of raw materials. Together with the contemporary ''[[Engineering (magazine)|Engineering]]'' journal the work is considered a valuable historical resource for the study of British economic history.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.eylhs.org.uk/railway.pdf|title=Railway History and the Local Historian|author=E.H. Fowkes|year=1963|work=East Yorkshire Local History Series|number=16|publisher=East Yorkshire Local History Society|page=40|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714130048/http://www.eylhs.org.uk/railway.pdf|archive-date=14 July 2014|df=dmy-all}}</ref> Early editors included Vaughan Pendred (1865–1905), [[Loughnan St Lawrence Pendred]] (1905–46) and Benjamin Pendred (from 1946).<ref>{{citation |title=Mr. L. St. L. Pendred |newspaper=[[The Times]] |issue=52785 |page=8 |date=21 November 1953}}</ref><ref>{{citation |title=Family's 100 years of editing |newspaper=[[The Times]] |issue=56483 |page=7 |date=19 November 1965}}</ref>

On 10 July 2012 the magazine announced its final print edition, the editor Jon Excell citing "increasing distribution and production costs, and the impact of an ongoing economic crisis on advertising revenues [which] have conspired to create a challenging environment for magazine publishers".<ref>{{citation|journal=The Engineer|title= Moving on(line)|author=Jon Excell|page=5|quote=After 156 year of chronicling the highlights of UK engineering innovation, this is the final fortnightly print edition of ''The Engineer'' magazine}}</ref> The owner of ''The Engineer'', Centaur Media proposed to focus the magazine’s editorial and commercial resources on growing the website, which had relaunched in 2009, and other digital products. According to Excell, demand for the print edition was such that after a 12-month hiatus, ''The Engineer'' returned as a monthly print magazine in September 2013.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.theengineer.co.uk/issues/july-2012-online/an-important-announcement-about-the-future-of-the-engineer/|author=Jon Excell|title=An important announcement about the future of The Engineer|access-date=8 February 2019|archive-date=4 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104014743/https://www.theengineer.co.uk/issues/july-2012-online/an-important-announcement-about-the-future-of-the-engineer/|url-status=dead}}</ref> As of 2019, ''The Engineer'' publishes 10 issues a year and has a presence on social media and the news aggregator Flipboard. The magazine runs an annual conference for the industry and an annual awards ceremony for the encouragement of collaboration in innovation.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.theengineer.co.uk/collaborate-to-innovate-awards-2018/|title=Collaborate to Innovate Awards}}</ref> ''The Engineer'' was acquired from Centaur Media by the Mark Allen Group in June 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pressgazette.co.uk/centaur-media-sells-engineering-titles-to-mark-allen-group-as-profits-climb/ |title=Centaur Media sells engineering titles to Mark Allen Group as profits climb |last=Walker |first=James |date=9 May 2019 |website=Press Gazette |language=en-US |access-date=31 October 2019}}</ref>
